title: Winners are investing more despite an uncertain macroeconomic outlook.
why_it_works: The "despite" clause turns a plain fact into a contrarian signal that tells the reader to act against the cycle.
watch_out: Progressive verb ("are investing") and "more" has no number or baseline; the chart holds 69% vs 36%.

title: Buyers expect omnichannel: Most decision makers use ten or more distinct channels to interact with suppliers along the journey.
why_it_works: A short claim first, then the quantified proof after the colon. The reader gets the point and the evidence in one line.
watch_out: Uses a colon to join two clauses, and the line runs to 19 words.
reuse_template: [Audience] expect [behavior]: [Most of segment] [do] [n or more units] to [purpose] [scope].

title: Volume growth has eluded consumer-packaged-goods companies in recent years.
why_it_works: A strong verb ("eluded") states a problem in nine words, and it sets up the price-versus-volume story.
watch_out: No number in the title; the chart carries the price vs volume split (e.g. 2023: +7.4 price, -1.3 volume).

title: One in five respondents report that their organizations’ use of AI has been constrained by their operating costs, including tokens.

parts.text: that their organizations’ use of AI
by their operating costs, including tokens

why_it_works: "One in five" is easy to picture, and the cause (token costs) is specific and new.
watch_out: Passive voice and a nested "report that" clause make the line long (20 words).
reuse_template: [n in m] [population] report that [activity] has been constrained by [cause].

title: Larger companies are moving from experimentation to scaling AI agents much faster than smaller ones.

parts.text: are moving from experimentation to scaling AI agents

pattern: [Subject] [verb: from state A to state B] [comparison].
why_it_works: It frames the finding as a gap between two named groups, so the reader sees who is ahead at once.
watch_out: Two -ing words ("moving", "scaling") and "much faster" has no number.
reuse_template: [Segment A] are moving from [stage 1] to [stage 2] much faster than [segment B].

title: Only 5% of Companies Get Substantial Value from AI, While 60% Lag in Developing Critical AI Capabilities

parts.text: While 60% Lag in Developing Critical AI Capabilities

pattern: Only [x% of population] [verb] [outcome], While [y%] [lag on capability]
why_it_works: Two hard numbers frame the full spread of the market: a thin top and a large tail. "Only" signals the gap.
watch_out: Two clauses and an -ing word ("Developing"); "Substantial" is not defined in the title.
reuse_template: Only [x%] of [population] [achieve outcome], While [y%] [lag in capability]

title: 70% of AI’s Value Is Concentrated in Core Businesses
why_it_works: It leads with the number. Eight words tell the reader where to point the AI investment.
watch_out: Passive verb; the chart subtitle says this is value potential, not realized value.

title: To Get an AI Transformation Right, 70% of the Focus Should Be on People and Processes

parts.text: To Get an AI Transformation Right

why_it_works: It gives a clear rule with a number, and it opens with the goal the reader already has.
watch_out: It states a prescriptive model (BCG 10-20-70), not a measured result, so a reader can take it as data.
reuse_template: To [achieve goal], [x%] of [effort] Should Be on [area]

title: Global AuM Grew by 12% in 2024 to $128 Trillion
why_it_works: It gives both the rate and the absolute level, so the reader gets growth and scale in nine words.
watch_out: Acronym (AuM) and no cause or implication; it reports, it does not argue.

title: Profits Rose in 2024 as Revenue Growth Outstripped Costs
why_it_works: It gives the result and the mechanism in nine words, so the chart only has to prove it.
watch_out: No number for the rise; the PDF text uses an "fi" ligature in "Profits", normalized here.
reuse_template: [Outcome metric] [moved] in [period] as [driver A] Outstripped [driver B]

title: Challenger Banks’ Average Deposits Are Lower, but Growing Faster Than Traditional Retail Banks

parts.text: but Growing Faster Than Traditional Retail Banks

pattern: [Subject] [verb: current state], but [trend comparison vs baseline]
why_it_works: It admits the weak point (lower level) and then gives the stronger point (faster growth), which reads as balanced.
watch_out: No numbers, and "Growing" is an -ing form; the baseline applies to both claims but appears only once.
reuse_template: [Challenger metric] Is Lower, but Growing Faster Than [incumbent]

title: Leaders run 8.5 times more AI experiments than laggards
why_it_works: Nine words, an active verb, a precise multiple and a named baseline. It is the canonical comparison title.
watch_out: "Leaders" and "laggards" are defined only in the body; the link to results is correlational.
reuse_template: [Top group] [do] [n times more X] than [bottom group]

title: Marketing leaders are two times more likely to realize revenue and cost benefits from AI initiatives

parts.text: to realize revenue and cost benefits

why_it_works: It ties the group to a business outcome (revenue and cost), not to an activity, with a clear multiple.
watch_out: The baseline is implicit ("more likely" than whom?); "two times" is spelled out, not shown as a number.
reuse_template: [Top group] are [n] times more likely to [realize outcome] from [initiative]

title: About 80% of search users rely on AI summaries at least 40% of the time
why_it_works: It quantifies both reach and intensity, so the size of the behavior shift is clear without the chart.
watch_out: Two percentages in one line, so a reader can mix up the 80% and the 40%.
reuse_template: About [x%] of [users] rely on [new channel] at least [y%] of the time

title: Sales growth was primarily driven by price in 2023
why_it_works: It isolates the single driver behind a headline metric, which is the decomposition an executive asks for first.
watch_out: Passive voice and no number; the share of growth from price lives only in the chart.
reuse_template: [Metric] growth was primarily driven by [driver] in [period]

title: Customer switching rates have risen as digital tools and more transparent pricing make it easier to defect

parts.text: as digital tools and more transparent pricing make it easier to defect

why_it_works: It pairs the trend with its two causes, so the reader knows what to address, not only what happened.
watch_out: No number for the rise, and the long cause clause makes the line 17 words.
reuse_template: [Risk metric] has risen as [driver A] and [driver B] make it easier to [undesired action]

title: Firms that obtain price increases will realize stronger margins
why_it_works: The subject is defined by an action the reader controls, so the title reads as a direct call to act.
watch_out: Future tense and no number; "stronger" needs the chart to show how much.
reuse_template: [Firms that do X] will realize [better outcome]
